transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Yeah, so… the main thing is I keep getting pulled off whatever I’m doing. It’s been maybe the past year or so that I’ve really noticed it. Like, my phone buzzes, or someone walks past my office door, or honestly even some random thought pops in—like something about my in-laws, which is a whole other story—and suddenly I’m not on the thing I was supposed to be doing anymore. It happens before I even catch myself, and it’s been frustrating enough that I figured I should come in.
Do you find yourself feeling restless, fatigued, or irritable, especially when you’re trying to focus or after these distractions happen?

Yeah, restless more than anything. Like if I’m supposed to just sit still — family dinners, or those church volunteer meetings where everyone’s going around the table — I feel like there’s a motor running in me. I’ll be tapping my foot, messing with a pen, folding a napkin, whatever’s nearby.  

It’s not even that I’m trying to be rude, I just get this “I need to move or do something” feeling. And then I’ll start thinking about, like, whether we parked in the right place or if I forgot to text someone back, but… yeah, the main thing is I feel wound up when I’m expected to sit there.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

I don’t think so… not like that, where it suddenly hits and I’m terrified or can’t breathe. I mean, I get worked up sometimes, like if I’m late and traffic is bad—actually the highway by my office is ridiculous lately, they’ve had cones out for weeks and I don’t even know what they’re doing—but that’s more irritation than fear.  

So yeah, no, I haven’t really noticed episodes like what you’re describing.
Have you noticed feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like you’re not good enough, especially around the same time these distractions and restlessness happen?

I don’t know that I’d say that, no. I mean, I get annoyed with myself when I’m bouncing around between things, like “why can’t I just finish this one email,” but I wouldn’t call it feeling down exactly.

Losing interest… not really? If anything I still want to do stuff, I just get pulled off it. Like I’ll start one thing and then remember something about the house, or my wife will mention we’re out of something, and then I’m looking up grocery delivery instead of doing what I was doing. But that’s not the same as not enjoying things, I don’t think.

And “not good enough”… I mean, everybody has moments, right? But I haven’t really noticed it being tied to all this in some big way.
Have you found yourself acting without thinking, like interrupting others, blurting things out, or starting new tasks before finishing old ones?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I do that. My wife would probably say I do it more than I think. I’ll jump into conversations, like when she’s on the phone with her parents or talking to them and I’ll just sort of answer something or add my opinion before anybody asked me.  

And at work, I catch myself finishing an employee’s sentence, like I already know where they’re going with it, and then I can see on their face they didn’t love that. I don’t mean it badly, I just… it comes out before I really stop and think.

Do you find it especially hard to stay focused or control your impulses in situations that require you to pay close attention or wait your turn, like in meetings, during conversations, or when reading something important?

Yeah, especially if I have to really stay with something. Like I can start a planning document or sit down with one of my managers and I’m good for the first few minutes, totally following along.

But then pretty soon I realize I missed half of what they said, and I’m sitting there trying to piece it together from the last sentence or whatever. Sometimes I have to ask them to run it back, which is embarrassing, because I was right there in front of them.

It’s not like I don’t care. I’m trying to pay attention, but my mind just kind of… slips off somewhere.
